conventions.testing: Unit tests in language modules; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs; test functions parse code snippets and assert on extracted elements

patterns: Language handler module exports ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY constants
extract_inheritance(node, source) -> Vec<String> returns formatted strings like 'extends Base' and 'implements Interface'
Tree-sitter queries use named captures (@capture_name) and @function/@class tags for element classification
Language wired in: mod.rs pub mod declaration, EXTENSION_MAP entry, Cargo.toml workspace dependency, get_language_info match arm, get_ts_language match arm
DEFUSE_QUERY captures write sites (local_variable_declaration, assignment) and read sites (identifier @read.usage)
constraints: PHP has no trait keyword (unlike Rust/Swift); uses interfaces and abstract classes for polymorphism
PHP grammar defines base_clause and class_interface_clause as unnamed children, not fields (unlike Java's superclass/interfaces fields)
PHP enums support backing types (int/string) and can implement interfaces
tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 is latest stable; grammar covers heredoc/nowdoc, anonymous classes, attributes
test_coverage: Integration tests verify: element extraction (methods, classes, interfaces, enums), import extraction, inheritance extraction, defuse sites (write/read). Each language test creates temp file, writes code snippet, calls analyze_file, asserts on output.semantic fields.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Minimal PHP handler (CSS-like, no inheritance)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY. No extract_inheritance handler. Register in mod.rs and lang.rs. Add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Full PHP handler with inheritance extraction
approaches.description: Add php.rs with all queries plus extract_inheritance() handler. Walk class_declaration node to find base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) children. Return formatted strings. Add comprehensive tests. Register in mod.rs, lang.rs, and Cargo.toml.
pros: Better for call graph and refactoring analysis
cons: Requires understanding PHP grammar field structure

approaches.name: Approach 3: PHP handler with optional trait support
approaches.description: Full handler (Approach 2) plus trait_declaration in ELEMENT_QUERY if grammar supports it. Extract trait requirements via class_interface_clause. Add tests for trait usage patterns. Verify grammar includes trait_declaration node type.
pros: Future-proof if PHP adds native traits
Comprehensive coverage of all declaration kinds
cons: Requires grammar verification (may not exist yet)
Adds complexity if trait support incomplete

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP handler with inheritance extraction). It balances completeness with implementation complexity, follows the established pattern from Java/Swift/C#, and provides the inheritance tracking needed for call graph analysis. The DEFUSE_QUERY is required because semantic analysis depends on it for def-use tracking in refactoring tasks.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-php grammar (php/src/node-types.json and common/define-grammar.js): class_declaration node has no parent_class or interfaces fields. Instead, it has unnamed children: base_clause (for extends) and class_interface_clause (for implements). Walk class_declaration's children; when encountering base_clause, extract its name child and format as 'extends Name'; when encountering class_interface_clause, extract each name child and format as 'implements Name'.
